prompt:
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: A velocity-time graph with a straight line that starts at (0 s, 18 m s^-1) and ends at (6.0 s, 6.0 m s^-1).]
What is the acceleration of the object?

answer.explanation: Acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph: a = Delta v / Delta t = (6.0 - 18) / (6.0 - 0) = -12 / 6.0 = -2.0 m s^-2.

distractor_explanations: Omits the negative sign; the line slopes downwards, so acceleration must be negative.
Divides initial velocity by time: 18 / 6.0 = 3.0 m s^-2.
hints: Acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph.
Delta v = final velocity - initial velocity = 6.0 - 18.
teacher_walkthrough: The downward slope confirms that acceleration is negative.
